extra_misconceptions.fact: Recipients can capture screenshots immediately, and remote servers often retain cached backups long after a user deletes a post.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Deleting an embarrassing photo or message from a social media app permanently erases every copy from the internet.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Incognito mode only prevents the local device from saving browsing history; websites and networks still log your IP address and traffic.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Private or incognito browser windows hide your identity and online messages from websites and internet providers.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Imposters frequently scrape public photos and add mutual contacts to build convincing fake profiles that deceive young users.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Online accounts displaying a teenager's profile photo and mutual friends are always operated by real peers.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Engaging escalates harassment; Scouts should stop replying immediately, save screenshots as evidence, block the sender, and tell an adult.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Replying to a cyberbully or predator to demand that they stop is the safest way to resolve online harassment.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to share photos containing embedded GPS EXIF metadata on public social profiles?
Under what condition does an online conversation cross the boundary into grooming or coercion?
What steps preserve digital evidence if a Scout receives a threatening or inappropriate message?
Which privacy settings prevent strangers from viewing your real-time location or personal contact info?

extra_misconceptions.fact: First-generation computers used thousands of vacuum tubes for logic and relied on paper punch cards and plugboards for input and output.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Early electronic computers like ENIAC stored data on magnetic hard drives and displayed output on video monitors.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Moore's Law is an empirical observation about transistor density on integrated circuits, and heat limits have slowed clock speed gains.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Moore's Law is a physical law of nature that guarantees computer processor clock speeds will double every two years.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Packet-switched networks like ARPANET began in the late 1960s, while Tim Berners-Lee created the World Wide Web protocols around 1990.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The World Wide Web and the internet were invented at the same time as a single communication system.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A single modern smartphone processor executes billions of instructions per second, millions of times faster than the Apollo Guidance Computer.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Modern smartphones have less raw computing power than the mainframe computers used during the Apollo moon landings.

extra_socratic_questions: What physical limitation caused vacuum tube computers to fail much more often than solid-state transistor systems?
In what way did replacing wired transistors with silicon integrated circuits change computer size and power draw?
Which architectural shift allowed computers to move from room-sized mainframes to portable personal devices?
What physical constraints limit how many microscopic transistors engineers can pack onto a silicon chip today?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Lossy compression permanently discards data during encoding, so converting to a lossless format never restores the discarded detail.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Converting a low-quality MP3 or JPEG file into a lossless format like WAV or PNG restores the original lost detail.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Stretching an existing bitmap only enlarges or interpolates existing pixels without capturing any new optical detail from the scene.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Increasing the pixel dimensions of a digital image by stretching it on screen increases its true optical resolution.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Analog-to-digital converters sample the sound wave thousands of times per second and quantize each sample into binary numbers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Digital audio recorders store continuous smooth sound waves directly inside flash memory chips.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Lossless compression replaces repeated byte patterns with shorter tokens so the exact original file can be reconstructed bit for bit.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Lossless compression algorithms like ZIP reduce file sizes by throwing away unimportant characters and numbers.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to an executable program or spreadsheet if you compress and decompress it using a lossy algorithm?
What measurement confirms whether an audio sampling rate is high enough to capture a specific sound frequency?
Why does encoding text in Unicode UTF-8 support international alphabets that 7-bit ASCII cannot represent?
Under what condition does saving a photograph as a JPEG introduce visible blocky artifacts around sharp edges?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Drives provide persistent long-term storage, whereas RAM is high-speed volatile working memory that holds active instructions for the CPU.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Adding a larger hard drive or solid-state drive increases the amount of active RAM available for running apps.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Attackers create new malware variants daily, so security software requires regular signature updates and OS patches to detect new exploits.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Antivirus software that was installed two years ago without updates still blocks modern zero-day malware threats.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A Trojan disguises itself as legitimate software and relies on a user to download and launch the program before it can execute its payload.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Trojan horse malware spreads automatically across local networks without any user interaction or file execution.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Every operating system contains software vulnerabilities and can be compromised by phishing, malicious apps, or unpatched browser exploits.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Mac, Linux, and mobile operating systems are immune to malware and never require security updates or caution.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to unsaved data held in volatile RAM if a computer suddenly loses electrical power?
Why must the operating system load program instructions from solid-state storage into RAM before the CPU runs them?
Which behavioral difference distinguishes a self-replicating network worm from a file-infecting computer virus?
Why is it dangerous to pay a ransomware demand without having an offline backup and patched security vulnerabilities?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wireless signals only bridge the short hop to a local router or cell tower, after which undersea and underground fiber-optic cables carry data.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wi-Fi and cellular data connections carry internet traffic all the way across the world without using physical cables.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Search rankings reflect keyword relevance, link popularity, or paid advertising rather than independent verification of factual accuracy.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The top result returned by an internet search engine is always the most accurate and trustworthy source on a topic.

extra_misconceptions.fact: HTTPS only encrypts data in transit; phishing sites routinely obtain valid TLS certificates for deceptive domain names.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An HTTPS padlock icon in the browser address bar proves that the website owner is honest and safe from phishing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: TCP/IP breaks data into small numbered packets that route independently across hops and reassemble in order at the destination device.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Internet data travels from sender to receiver as a single unbroken stream over a dedicated circuit like a phone call.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a large file transfer when routers split it into IP packets that travel along different network paths?
Which physical indicator and protocol verify that a website encrypts your login credentials during transit?
Under what condition does a fiber-optic cable transmit data much farther and faster than a twisted-pair copper wire?
Why is it dangerous to log into banking or email accounts over an unencrypted public Wi-Fi hotspot?

extra_misconceptions.fact: If that single drive fails or is lost, both folders disappear; true backups must reside on separate physical media or off-site storage.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Saving a second copy of a project file in a different folder on the same hard drive protects it as a true backup.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Operating systems cache writes in memory, so pulling a drive before using safe eject can corrupt the file system and ruin the backup.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Unplugging an external USB flash drive while a file transfer is still writing data is safe once the progress bar hits 99%.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Typing text symbols into cells can turn numbers into text strings that formulas ignore; store raw numbers and apply currency formatting.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Formatting numbers with dollar signs by typing text characters into spreadsheet cells still allows math formulas to sum them.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Uncompressed images bloat presentation file sizes and slow down rendering without adding detail beyond the projector's native resolution.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Embedding high-resolution uncompressed photos into a slide deck always improves projection quality without any downside.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a campout budget total if you type a static number instead of a dynamic SUM formula in a cell?
Where should a Scout store a secondary backup copy so a single lost USB drive does not erase all project files?
Which spreadsheet reference style keeps a tax or per-camper rate cell locked when you copy a formula down a column?
What verification step confirms that files copied to an external backup drive can actually be opened on another PC?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Copyright protection attaches automatically the moment an original work is fixed in a tangible medium, even without a copyright notice.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any image, song, or program found on a public website without a copyright symbol is in the public domain and free to copy.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Commercial software purchases grant a limited End User License Agreement for specific devices, not ownership or redistribution rights.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Buying a commercial software application gives you the legal right to install copies on all of your friends' computers.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Freeware costs nothing to run but usually keeps its source code closed and forbids modification, unlike open-source licenses.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Freeware and open-source software are identical because both let users modify the source code and sell copies freely.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A patent requires full public disclosure of how the invention works in exchange for a temporary legal monopoly to exclude copycats.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Registering a patent keeps an invention's technical design hidden from the public so competitors cannot study it.

extra_socratic_questions: Under what condition is it legal to accept and install a free copy of a software program from a friend?
Which legal protection covers a functional invention mechanism rather than the source code or brand logo?
What happens to a company's trade secret protection if a competitor independently reverse-engineers the product?
Why does a Creative Commons or open-source license still require users to follow attribution or share-alike rules?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Curbside bins are built for paper, glass, and cans; lithium batteries in e-waste frequently spark fires inside sorting trucks and plants.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tossing old cell phones and circuit boards into a municipal curbside recycling bin ensures they are recycled safely.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard deletion only removes file pointers, so recovery tools can read private data until the drive is securely overwritten or wiped.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dragging personal files to the desktop trash can or recycle bin removes your private data before donating a computer.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Uncertified collectors often ship e-waste overseas for open-air burning; look for R2 or e-Stewards certification to verify safe processing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: All companies advertising free electronics drop-off dismantle toxic components safely inside regulated domestic facilities.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Electronic devices still contain hazardous substances like lead solder, cadmium, mercury, and brominated flame retardants.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Modern flat-screen devices and circuit boards contain only harmless plastics and aluminum with no toxic heavy metals.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to crush or puncture a swollen lithium-ion battery inside a discarded smartphone or laptop?
What happens to groundwater when lead solder, mercury, and cadmium from landfilled circuit boards leach into soil?
Which third-party certification confirms that an electronics recycler processes hazardous e-waste safely and legally?
What data sanitization step must a Scout complete before donating or recycling an old computer or mobile phone?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many network, cloud, and cybersecurity roles hire candidates with associate degrees, apprenticeships, or vendor certifications.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every high-paying digital technology career requires a four-year university degree in computer science before you can get hired.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Entry-level pay is typically in the lower quartile of national medians and varies widely by local cost of living and credentials.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: National average salary figures represent the exact starting paycheck a newly hired entry-level technician will earn in any city.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Industrial facilities also rely on programmable logic controllers, barcode scanners, automated sensors, and inventory systems.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Digital technology in an industrial facility is limited to the desktop computers and laptops inside the main administrative office.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Digital professionals must complete continuing education and renew technical certifications every few years to keep up with new systems.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Initial technical training is enough to sustain a digital career for decades without ongoing study or credential renewal.

extra_socratic_questions: Under what condition may a Scout conduct an online interview or visit a digital technology workplace for career research?
Which credential difference separates an accredited degree from a vendor certification for entry-level IT roles?
What measurement in the Occupational Outlook Handbook confirms whether a digital career has growing 10-year job demand?
Why is it dangerous to photograph proprietary screens or touch server racks without clearance during a workplace facility tour?
